::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 1st 1872  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels
:::

My dear [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd)
I like this very much and Gruet is a very satisfactory Eagle.[^1]  It is much more satisfactory to reform Ruprecht instead of demolishing him-  The land of romance too is a satisfactory variety.  There is one [fairy land play](other_books/otherbook_821.qmd) – also a [story from Gibraltar](other_books/otherbook_822.qmd) and [one from Ascension isle](other_books/otherbook_819.qmd) and [one](other_books/otherbook_817.qmd) from [Mme de Witt](people/person_423.qmd) about a poor girl left in charge of her sisters children while their parents are shut up in Paris! [^2]  Also a [Church decking narrative](other_books/otherbook_820.qmd) related by a Church Eagle, who certainly does not shew himself at all a goose.  But I have three visits – only one is a boy’s, which makes a little variety.

I suppose it is too late now for the suggestion but should you not call Ferdinand the [Constant Prince](other_books/otherbook_741.qmd) to make plain whom you mean

your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: CMy refers to the plans for the Christmas number of the *MP* for 1872, to which Coleridge contributed a story called 'Minne's Knight'.
[^2]: Inserted above, 'young lady'.
